FYM split 49% DPM 49% RPM 2% HUM
Weighted aggregate score represents user preference not biological truth
RothC clay-dependent CO2 versus retained-carbon partition with retained carbon routed 46% BIO and 54% HUM; supersedes the Phase 2 all-respiration scaffold
Official-compatible post-decomposition external carbon input timing is the Phase 4 default; explicit legacy_pre_decomposition mode preserves Phase 3 input-bearing trajectory reproducibility
WOFOST EU15 spring-barley daytime-temperature assimilation response is linearly interpolated against monthly mean air temperature
RothC moisture modifier is linearly rescaled from its configured 0.2-1.0 range to a 0-1 plant water-stress modifier
Plant P stress equals the fraction of configured whole-plant tissue-P demand met by the available-P pool; uptake is capped by demand and stock
Realised NPP uses multiplicative bounded temperature water and P stress then a fixed configured shoot-root partition
Configured harvest index residue-retention and root-residue fractions determine grain export biomass export and residue return
Whole-plant dry matter is converted with a fixed carbon fraction of 0.45
Decomposed AMF necromass routes to the protected proxy at the existing provisional 0.15 fraction and the remaining carbon is split between DPM and RPM using the configured RothC crop ratio

CUE-derived AMF respiration is operationally split into maintenance associated with replacing current turnover and growth associated with net biomass expansion without a separate maintenance coefficient
Direct-root and AMF phosphorus pathways use separate aggregate Michaelis-Menten kinetics while withdrawing from one available-P stock; the root half-saturation scale is provisional
Plant temperature and RothC-derived plant moisture modifiers are reused for AMF phosphorus acquisition and carbon allocation and AMF acquisition is inactive without configured potential host growth
Beneficial neutral and harmful labels compare net plant carbon and yield against a parallel deterministic no-AMF counterfactual and are model implications rather than causal agronomic claims
FYM phosphorus content is represented by a provisional configurable kg P per t C conversion while carbon uses the established RothC 49/49/2 route

Conventional reduced and no-till events use provisional pulse mortality turnover decomposition cover-suppression duration and standing-biomass incorporation parameters; literature supports direction not magnitude
A generic deterministic AMF-compatible cover crop uses provisional monthly NPP root allocation water-use residue-return and P-return parameters and is not species or site calibrated
Same-month events execute in the documented P application then tillage then cover termination then manure staging then cover establishment order with event ID tie-breaking
Intervention costs and kg CO2e emissions proxies are additive event metadata and do not alter mechanistic carbon or phosphorus stocks
Cover-plant P is carried explicitly and returned or exported at termination while crop uptake has priority in overlapping months; no mineralisation delay or unavailable-P chemistry is represented
Texture perturbation uses an additive-log-ratio transform around each empirical seed so clay silt and sand remain positive and sum to 100 percent
A shared Gaussian soil factor and bounded residuals preserve provisional positive SOC-CEC-N and negative SOC-bulk-density dependence around joint seeds
Initial AMF live and necromass stocks use bounded log-scale perturbation with a provisional negative available-P coupling while retaining management-history context
RothC active pools use periodic complete-weather-sequence spin-up under a reference historical carbon input then linear scaling to target SOC after IOM and AMF stocks
Phase 7 finite range and impossible-combination QC limits define a conservative mineral arable topsoil model domain and are not calibrated national distribution limits
Cover-crop establishment success is drawn and recorded as a future aleatory latent but does not alter deterministic Phase 6 cover-crop execution

Field-specific configuration expands the AMF turnover validation ceiling only for the compound sampled base turnover times configured tillage multiplier; the base draw remains 0.1-6 per month and equations are unchanged
The bundled Phase 7 joint seed and complete-weather-year records are versioned deterministic local research fixtures for adapter and generator verification not a representative empirical UK sample

The primary observable feature registry treats configured soil weather management and metadata variables as pre-intervention measurements while excluding IDs archetypes latent biological draws and hidden initial simulator pools

Validation-group split-conformal absolute residuals provide marginal intervals under synthetic exchangeability and do not quantify simulator structural error mechanistic epistemic uncertainty or real-field uncertainty

Deterministic field-level feature permutation is used to diagnose dependence on engineered clay-SOC SOC-bulk-density and available-P-AMF generator correlations without asserting those relationships are empirically false

Regularisation tree ensemble and validation selection grids are explicit non-biological benchmark choices and the frozen test groups do not tune preprocessing models hyperparameters or interval widths

Phase 8.5 expands ten local demonstration templates into 50 distinct synthetic non-representative seed groups using permuted soil donors independent residual variation and diversified soil climate management and AMF combinations

The Phase 8.5 shared soil-factor SD is 0.035 the SOC-bulk-density shared coefficient is 0.10 independent SOC log SD is 0.11 independent bulk-density SD is 0.075 g cm-3 and AMF log SD is 0.32; these revise fixture covariance but are not field-calibrated

Training validation final-test complete-archetype-OOD and extreme-weather-OOD partitions are assigned at empirical-seed-group level and final/OOD outcomes cannot tune preprocessing models hyperparameters or intervals
Crop-yield targets use 24 months while carbon-stock protected-proxy and respiration direct/effect targets use 60 and 120 months; existing Phase 6 event dates are retained without automatic repetition

Observable features are limited to soil-test-like measurements baseline total SOC weather summaries management history coarse phosphorus status policy and horizon; raw simulator available P hidden pools spin-up state labels IDs and biological draws remain diagnostic only

Group-aware uncertainty uses one residual quantile per validation empirical-seed group followed by a conformal group rank and abstains from calibration claims below configured group or subgroup counts

Phase 9 requires nonlinear primary effect error below policy mean and the best pooled or separate-policy ridge plus leakage uncertainty and OOD gates; v0.8.5 fails the regularised-linear comparison so selector development is blocked

Phase 8.6 treats policy mean pooled ridge separate-policy ridge pooled forest and separate-policy forest as predeclared candidates and selects the least complex model within 5 percent of the best median validation normalised RMSE; ridge is a legitimate ML model and nonlinear complexity has no preference

Phase 8.6 repeats ten independently seeded synthetic foundations and populations while weather-resampling and latent-biological seed streams are controlled separately; the repeated fixtures remain non-representative and do not add empirical field evidence
Phase 8.6 weather OOD groups apply coherent dry hot wet cool and compound hot-dry whole-year perturbations with configured temperature rainfall and PET multipliers solely for synthetic stress testing

Phase 8.6 uncertainty widths are calibrated separately for each primary paired-effect target and weather regime using independent development groups; target-regime pairs exceeding the error threshold or lacking 20 calibration groups abstain

The Phase 8.6 applicability domain is frozen from repeated development and calibration evidence before a new final population is instantiated; final outcomes cannot alter models hyperparameters intervals support decisions or gates

Phase 9 readiness in v0.8.6 requires consistent improvement over policy mean stable repeated-seed error acceptable untouched-final error calibrated or abstaining uncertainty and support in at least three dedicated weather regimes; nonlinear models need not beat ridge
Phase 9 utility profiles and every objective weight carbon-horizon mixture and hard threshold are explicit user-adjustable synthetic scenario choices rather than agronomic recommendations
Phase 9 objective means and scales policy means and best-global policies are fitted only on new train and validation groups; untouched repeated and frozen-final outcomes cannot tune them
Catastrophic failure is predeclared as normalised feasible-oracle regret at least 0.50 or any revealed hard-constraint violation
The frozen Phase 9 observable numeric domain requires each feature within eight Phase 8.6 training standard deviations and known categorical levels in addition to target-weather support
A Phase 9 abstention remains a null selection and baseline is used only as an explicit post-selection evaluation action for regret accounting; it is never presented as a recommendation
The transparent benchmark rule uses only coarse phosphorus status tillage-history intensity and cover-history indicator with fixed ordering and has no agronomic-validity claim

Uncertainty-aware selectors propagate frozen Phase 8.6 marginal synthetic residual widths into conservative utility and constraints; the intervals exclude causal mechanistic structural-model and real-field uncertainty

Phase 9 stress tests permute observable generator relationships diagnose latent draws only after selection scale interval widths without refitting and move conventional-tillage decomposition multiplier across its registered range without selector recalibration

Phase 9.5 cost and emissions proxies accrue only on explicit recurring events at 24 60 and 120 months; operational and partial lifecycle components remain separate and provisional rather than regional budgets or complete LCAs
The biologically null no_till marker is removed from the Phase 9.5 benchmark policy set because it is exactly identical to baseline in the audited equations

Phase 9.5 headline ML targets are paired intervention-minus-baseline yield total-SOC protected-SOC-proxy and respiration effects at predeclared horizons; stock levels remain circularity diagnostics only
Cost and emissions values are deterministic schedule calculations and are excluded from ML fitting scoring and headline skill claims
The bounded phosphorus ablation uses 5 kg P ha-1 per scheduled event versus the current 20 kg P ha-1 without changing the plant-growth equation and is a scenario bound rather than calibration

The alternative phosphorus-response ablation raises the direct-uptake AMF-uptake and allocation half-saturation values to 40 kg P ha-1 and compares intervention with a matched alternative-parameter baseline

Phase 9.5 Morris screening and Sobol analysis use the complete registered ranges deterministic seeds and unit-hypercube elementary effects; the archived one-field result does not include empirical population-covariance propagation

The Hoosfield 1852 stocks initialise uncalibrated treatment trajectories while all later observations are validation data; official plant and FYM carbon schedules are used and the existing documented simulator temperature pattern remains an explicit forcing limitation

No Phase 9.5 empirical soil-climate population is claimed because a version-pinned paired extraction of at least 50 locations could not be obtained reliably; the existing ten-seed and Phase 8.6 fixtures remain synthetic
Observable soil-climate covariance is not re-estimated without sufficient real pilot records and deliberately imposed latent biological relationships remain separate and provisional
Phosphorus effect magnitudes are unresolved without a defensible calibration dataset and phosphorus is excluded from headline carbon-management conclusions
The normalized Hoosfield fixture preserves source treatment depth year stock units and preprocessing while its local SHA-256 and the upstream e-RA extraction SHA-256 are recorded separately

Phase 9.6 SoilGrids median predictions are harmonised by explicit layer thickness to 0--23 cm; layer SOC stock is concentration times bulk density times thickness and independently predicted texture fractions are renormalised with corrections retained
Available phosphorus AMF initial stocks drainage and management history are not observed by the paired pilot and remain separate provisional priors rather than empirical covariance variables

Phase 9.6 preserves observed between-location covariance by seeding fields from paired records while bounded within-location texture SOC bulk-density and pH perturbations remain explicit scenario assumptions and the authored shared covariance factor is disabled

NASA POWER monthly mean temperature drives Thornthwaite potential evapotranspiration with latitude and daylength; the existing PET-to-open-pan divisor remains an explicit scenario conversion because derived PET is not measured pan evaporation

Population sensitivity spans a bounded spin-up pool-allocation blend while preserving each field total carbon stock; this probes structural initialization uncertainty and is not a calibrated pool observation

The official RothC v2.1.1 bundled Hoosfield monthly normal replaces the Phase 9.5 authored weather pattern for source-corrected diagnosis without changing RothC turnover constants or treatment schedules

Optional Hoosfield calibration varies only plant-residue and FYM input-reconstruction factors within predeclared bounds using unmanured and annual-FYM observations through 1965; later years and the complete cessation treatment are held out and calibrated factors are not retained as general simulator parameters

Phase 9.6 ML targets are paired biological effects only; deterministic schedule cost and emissions remain metadata and downstream selector or regret analysis is fail-closed unless test OOD uncertainty and independent empirical effect-validation gates all pass

The original severity-labelled v0.9.0 external audit body was not present in the repository or supplied attachment; request-derived remediation items are tracked separately and unknown original findings cannot be declared closed
Phase 9.7 uses one scrambled SciPy Sobol sequence in 2D split into A and B matrices with Saltelli first-order and Jansen total-order estimators; negative finite-sample estimates are retained

Phase 9.7 convergence uses nested base samples 128 256 512 and 1024 with predeclared index-change rank-correlation confidence-width and unstable-fraction thresholds; failure prevents final sensitivity claims

Empirical-location leakage passes only when empirical seeds generated descendants preprocessing calibration and exact or near-duplicate field groups are computably isolated; missing evidence fails closed

Independent empirical effect validation requires an identified independent dataset of at least 30 observations covering every primary target and supported horizon and unused in calibration or model development; no such current dataset exists

Nominal 90 percent coverage is evaluated separately by target and test or OOD regime against the exact central 95 percent binomial count range with Wilson intervals and interval-width inflation diagnostics; undersized regimes abstain

The FYM carbon reconstruction factor remains bounded at 0.90 to 1.10; the 1.10 estimate is boundary-constrained and a decreasing edge objective implies likely improvement beyond the permitted range without authorising bound widening

The Phase 9.6 historical artifact manifest remains unchanged while a Phase 9.7 correction manifest records the current audit-document bytes every changed hash the reason for change and a new canonical set digest
